channel.title: Nobita Talks AI
channel.description: Focusing on AI foundation models and tech insights

item.title: Production InfiniBand Deployment, Cluster Operations, and NCCL Tuning: OFED Drivers, OpenSM HA, ibdiagnet Fabric Auditing, and GPUDirect RDMA
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: What bare-metal operational challenges arise when translating network architecture into physical 10,000-GPU AI data centers? A comprehensive guide to production InfiniBand operations: installing and managing Mellanox OFED / DOCA driver stacks and firmware tools (flint/mlxlink); configuring high-availability Master/Standby Subnet Manager topologies with OpenSM; auditing fabric health and diagnosing dirty optical links (Symbol Errors) and speed renegotiation drops using ibdiagnet; and diving into the GPU communication layer to configure GPUDirect RDMA (nvidia-peermem) and tune mission-critical NCCL parameters (NCCL_IB_HCA, NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=5) for wire-speed All-Reduce performance.

item.title: InfiniBand AI Cluster Networking in Practice: Fat-Tree Topologies, Rail-Optimized Architecture, Adaptive Routing (AR), and In-Network Reduction (SHARP)
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: How can thousands of 8-GPU servers be interconnected with tens of thousands of optical links into a non-blocking, deadlock-free high-performance fabric? Deconstruct modern AI supercluster topologies: from Charles Leiserson's 1985 Fat-Tree mathematical model and port count k derivations for 2-Tier and 3-Tier non-blocking ceilings to the 8-plane Rail-Optimized architecture tailored for DGX H100/H200/B200 clusters; analyze how FTree and Up/Down routing engines forbid 'Down-then-Up' turns to eliminate credit loop deadlocks; and discover how hardware Adaptive Routing (AR) and SHARP in-network aggregation achieve a 2x throughput boost during GPU All-Reduce operations.

item.title: InfiniBand Architecture First Principles: Physical Link Rates, Credit-Based Link Flow Control, and Subnet Manager Fabric Orchestration
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why does native InfiniBand remain the dominant fabric for 10,000-GPU AI compute clusters and top-tier supercomputers in 2026? Deconstruct the layered InfiniBand protocol stack and physical link evolution: from EDR 100G, HDR 200G, and NDR 400G (Quantum-2) to the 2026 mass production of XDR 800G (Quantum-X800/ConnectX-8); analyze link-layer first principles: Flit-level Credit-Based hardware flow control and sub-100ns Cut-Through switching mechanics; and explore the control engine: Subnet Manager (OpenSM) fabric discovery, dynamic GUID/LID/LMC allocation, and Linear Forwarding Table (LFT) hardware orchestration.

item.title: Linux Kernel Networking Subsystem in Depth: From NIC Drivers, NAPI, and Ring Buffers to eBPF XDP Wire-Speed Forwarding
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: How does an electrical pulse on an Ethernet cable transform into data inside application memory? Deconstruct the entire Linux operating system network protocol stack: from hardware NIC RX Ring Buffer descriptors and PCIe DMA zero-copy transfers to hardware interrupt handling, NAPI hybrid polling, and ksoftirqd softirq execution; analyze the pointer architecture and zero-copy lifecycle of Linux's core sk_buff data structure; optimize multi-core NICs via RSS hardware queues and RPS/RFS CPU affinity; and explore cutting-edge eBPF XDP (eXpress Data Path) mechanics for multi-million PPS wire-speed packet filtering and DDoS mitigation.

item.title: RDMA High-Performance Networking Foundations: Kernel Bypass, Zero-Copy, Queue Pairs, and Lossless RoCEv2 (PFC/ECN) Architecture
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why does the traditional TCP/IP stack become a compute black hole in 400G and 800G networks? Deconstruct RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) first principles: Kernel Bypass, hardware-level Zero-Copy, and Memory Registration (MR/L_Key/R_Key); dissect core ibverbs primitives: Queue Pairs (SQ/RQ), Completion Queues (CQ), and microsecond-level mechanics of Two-Sided (Send/Recv) vs One-Sided (RDMA Read/Write/Atomic) operations; and uncover how Lossless RoCEv2 (UDP port 4791) leverages 802.1Qbb Priority Flow Control (PFC) backpressure and ECN/DCQCN closed-loop congestion control to resolve packet loss collapse and deadlock.

item.title: Modern Data Center Network Architecture First Principles: Clos Topologies, Leaf-Spine Fabrics, BGP Underlay, and EVPN-VXLAN Large Layer-2 Virtualization
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why can't traditional three-tier architectures and Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) handle modern cloud computing and large-scale AI clusters? Deconstruct the evolution of data center networking: from classical 3-tier bottlenecks (Access, Aggregation, Core) with STP link blocking and oversubscription, to Charles Clos's 1953 telephone switching theory and modern non-blocking 2-Tier / 3-Tier Leaf-Spine mathematical modeling; analyze RFC 7938 eBGP Underlay routing designs, ECMP 5-tuple hash polarization hazards and ASIC-level solutions; and dissect large Layer-2 Overlay mechanics: VXLAN MAC-in-UDP encapsulation (24-bit VNI, 9000 MTU Jumbo Frames) and MP-BGP EVPN Type-2/Type-3/Type-5 control plane route signaling.

item.title: Application & Transport Layer Bridges: DNS Resolution, Sockets, Ports, and UDP vs TCP Foundations
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: When you type a web URL into a browser and press Enter, how do packets locate the target server across continents and enter the exact destination application process? Deconstruct the bridge connecting applications to the transport layer: explore the global DNS hierarchy (13 logical Root Server clusters with Anycast scaling, TLD registries, authoritative name servers, recursive vs iterative querying); derive the fundamentals of Ports and OS Sockets, explaining how a single server port 80 sustains one million concurrent connections via 5-tuples; and compare the core design trade-offs of the transport layer's twin pillars: lightweight 8-byte UDP datagrams vs connection-oriented 20-byte TCP byte streams.

item.title: Enterprise LAN Infrastructure: VLAN Segmentation (802.1Q), Dynamic DHCP, and NAT Port Forwarding
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why can a single physical network switch be carved into dozens of isolated virtual local networks? Deconstruct three core pillars of enterprise LAN engineering: from broadcast storm hazards to IEEE 802.1Q frame tagging (4-byte tag, 12-bit VID, PCP QoS priority); the operational differences between Access ports, Trunk ports, and PVID tag stripping/insertion; comparing router-on-a-stick sub-interfaces with Layer 3 Switch Virtual Interfaces (SVI); dissecting DHCP's 4-step DORA handshake and cross-subnet relay agents; and demystifying NAPT (Port Address Translation), SNAT, DNAT, and Linux kernel conntrack state tables.

item.title: TCP Congestion Control Evolution & High-Performance Transport: From Reno and Cubic to BBR Mathematical Models, and HTTP/2 to HTTP/3 (QUIC)
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why can sliding windows prevent buffer overflow at the peer receiver but fail to stop Internet backbone routers from collapsing? Deconstruct thirty years of congestion control evolution: from loss-based AIMD, Reno state machines, and Bufferbloat to the cubic polynomial mathematics of Linux's default Cubic algorithm; dissect Google BBR's physical modeling of maximum delivery rate and minimum round-trip propagation time (BtlBw/RTprop/Pacing Rate); and analyze the transport revolution from HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 Head-of-Line (HoL) blocking to UDP-based HTTP/3 (QUIC) 0-RTT handshakes and seamless connection migration.

item.title: IP Addressing and Subnetting First Principles: Binary Arithmetic, Subnet Masks, CIDR, and Default Gateway Routing
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why must computers worldwide rely on IP addresses even though every network interface card already has a unique physical MAC address? Deconstruct network layer first principles from scratch: the binary structure and dotted-decimal notation of IPv4; the mathematical mechanics of Subnet Masks and step-by-step bitwise AND derivations, using 192.168.1.130/26 to compute network ID, broadcast address, and usable host capacity (the 2^H - 2 rule); examine the limitations of legacy Classful addressing, CIDR prefixes, and RFC 1918 private scopes; and demystify how the Default Gateway strips and rewrites Layer 2 headers when routing packets across subnets.

item.title: Network & Transport Layers in Depth: IP Routing, CIDR, TCP 11-State Machine, and Sliding Window First Principles
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: How can an absolutely reliable, ordered stream of data be built on top of an unreliable physical network? Deconstruct core Layer 3 and Layer 4 mechanics: from IPv4/IPv6 packet structures and CIDR subnets to Linux kernel Longest Prefix Match (LPM) and FIB/RIB table lookups; dissect the classic 11 TCP state transitions, 3-way handshake mechanics, SYN Flood & SYN Cookies defense, 4-way teardown with TIME_WAIT rationale; and derive sliding window flow control, zero-window probing, and TCP_NODELAY production tuning from first principles.

item.title: Computer Networking from Scratch: Bits, Physical Media, Hub Collision Domains, and Switch MAC Addressing First Principles
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: If you know nothing about computer networking, how can you build an intuitive, solid first-principles foundation? Deconstruct network communication from absolute zero: how computers represent 0 and 1 via voltages and light pulses; why twisted pair copper cables are spiraled to cancel noise; single-mode vs multi-mode optical fiber physics; the legacy Hub era, shared media, collision domains, and CSMA/CD exponential backoff; how Layer 2 switches eliminate collisions using MAC address tables (CAM) and Ethernet frames; and dissect ARP broadcast requests, unicast replies, gratuitous ARP, and spoofing mitigation.

item.title: Container Networking Deep Dive: veth-pair, Linux Bridge, iptables NAT, and Cross-Host Topology
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: How do processes isolated within private Network Namespaces communicate with host networks and the external Internet? An in-depth teardown of container network packet forwarding: veth-pair virtual ethernet pipes, Linux Bridge (docker0) Layer-2 forwarding, iptables PREROUTING/POSTROUTING DNAT port forwarding and MASQUERADE SNAT, alongside a performance and architectural comparison across Host, Bridge, Macvlan, and Overlay cross-host topologies.

item.title: Docker Internals from First Principles: Linux Namespaces, cgroups v2, and OverlayFS Union Mounts Deep Dive
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why are containers not lightweight virtual machines, but ordinary Linux processes constrained by kernel views and resource quotas? An in-depth first-principles exploration of Docker's three core pillars: clone() system calls with the six Linux Namespaces, cgroups v2 single-hierarchy unified resource limits, and OverlayFS layered union mounts with Copy-on-Write (CoW), alongside the OCI, containerd, and runc execution chain.

item.title: Lightweight Cluster Orchestration: Docker SwarmKit Architecture, Raft Consensus, and Ingress Routing Mesh
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why do engineering teams still leverage Docker Swarm in the cloud-native era dominated by Kubernetes? An architectural deep dive into SwarmKit internals: Manager and Worker node topologies, built-in Raft consensus state machine, VXLAN-powered cross-host overlay networking, and kernel-level IPVS Ingress Routing Mesh service discovery, complete with production trade-offs between Swarm and Kubernetes.

item.title: Application Networking on Kubernetes: The gRPC Load Balancing Trap, Service Mesh, and Zero-Downtime Draining Sequences
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why do enterprise microservices migrated to Kubernetes frequently suffer from intermittent 502 Bad Gateway errors during rolling updates while gRPC workloads bottleneck onto a single Pod? A deep architectural exploration into application-layer networking on Kubernetes: why HTTP/2 multiplexing breaks Layer-4 ClusterIP load balancing and how Headless Services and Envoy resolve it; MaxConnectionAge, JVM DNS TTL -1 traps, and reconnect storms; the asynchronous race condition between Pod deletion and EndpointSlice propagation; and production zero-downtime draining sequences via preStop hooks, graceful shutdowns, and readinessGates.

item.title: Kubernetes Control Plane Deep Dive: Declarative APIs, etcd Consensus, Scheduler, and Controller Reconciliation Loops
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why have declarative APIs and modern control theory emerged as the definitive standard for cloud infrastructure? A comprehensive architectural deconstruction of the Kubernetes Control Plane: kube-apiserver request admission pipelines (Authentication, RBAC, Mutating and Validating Webhooks), etcd v3 MVCC revisions and Watch streams, kube-scheduler two-phase filter and score algorithms, Informer mechanics (Reflector, DeltaFIFO, Indexer, WorkQueue), and level-triggered controller reconciliation loops.

item.title: Hacking the Kubernetes Control Plane: WatchCache Internals, Aggregated APIServers, APF Shuffle Sharding, and 10k-Node etcd Sharding
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why do Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) overwhelm etcd and paralyze Kubernetes when custom object counts breach millions? A deep architectural guide to re-engineering the Kubernetes control plane: dissecting kube-apiserver's in-memory WatchCache ring buffers and the three resourceVersion semantics; implementing standalone Aggregated APIServers for external high-throughput database backends; analyzing the combinatorial mathematics behind API Priority and Fairness (APF) Shuffle Sharding; and deploying physical dual-disk NVMe isolation and event sharding for 10,000-node hyperscale clusters.

item.title: Production Databases and Storage on Kubernetes: Local NVMe Passthrough, RocksDB/WAL Tuning, and Fencing Split-Brain Protection
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why do enterprise engineering teams migrating databases to Kubernetes abandon cloud network block storage in favor of bare-metal Local NVMe SSDs? A comprehensive exploration of running stateful distributed storage on Kubernetes: overcoming cloud disk multi-hop latency bottlenecks with Local Persistent Volumes; XFS formatting tuning and resolving cgroups v2 OOM cascades caused by Linux page cache dirty page backlogs; RocksDB/MySQL WAL Direct I/O and fdatasync optimizations; and mitigating split-brain dual-primary corruption using hardware IPMI STONITH and lease-based Node Fencing.

item.title: 2026 AI Computing Infrastructure: Kubernetes GPU Operator, MIG Partitioning, Topology-Aware Scheduling, and Auto-scaling Inference Engines
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why does traditional CPU/memory scalar scheduling fail in the large language model era? A rigorous architectural deconstruction of AI infrastructure on Kubernetes in 2026: automated zero-touch lifecycles via the NVIDIA GPU Operator; hardware-isolated Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) slicing versus time-slicing; overcoming cross-NUMA interconnect bottlenecks with Kubelet Topology Manager and Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA); and production auto-scaling for vLLM and SGLang inference clusters leveraging KEDA and real-time KV cache saturation metrics.

item.title: Kubernetes Networking Panorama: CNI Specification, Calico BGP, Cilium eBPF, and Gateway API Architecture
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why is container networking widely regarded as the most intricate subsystem of Kubernetes? A deep architectural exploration into Kubernetes networking axioms and CNI (Container Network Interface) plugin execution lifecycles; rigorous comparisons between Flannel VXLAN overlays and Calico BGP underlay routing; how Cilium leverages Linux kernel eBPF and sockops socket redirection to bypass kube-proxy and iptables bottlenecks; and the role-oriented traffic governance of the modern Gateway API.

item.title: Kubernetes Extensibility: The Operator Pattern, Custom Resource Definitions (CRD), and KubeBuilder in Production
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why is the Operator pattern universally recognized as the decisive architectural breakthrough that crowned Kubernetes the operating system of the modern cloud? A comprehensive deconstruction of Operator philosophy: codifying senior SRE domain knowledge into software; how CRDs register dynamic endpoints in apiextensions-apiserver with /status and /scale subresource isolation; and an in-depth breakdown of Controller-Runtime and KubeBuilder architecture (Manager, Cache, Split Client, Reconcile, and Finalizers), complete with production Go code for high-availability distributed stateful middleware.

item.title: Hacking Kubernetes Nodes & Runtimes: Breaking PLEG Bottlenecks, NRI Plugins, Kata/gVisor Sandboxes, and cgroups v2 Tuning
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why do traditional runc containers sharing the host kernel fail against zero-day escapes, and why do dense worker nodes frequently freeze with 'PLEG is not healthy' errors? A deep architectural exploration of customizing Kubernetes worker nodes and container runtimes: analyzing Kubelet's syncLoop and the Evented PLEG streaming revolution; developing custom Go plugins using the containerd/CRI-O Node Resource Interface (NRI) for dynamic CPU pinning and OCI manipulation; contrasting Kata Containers microVMs against gVisor user-space kernel sandboxes; and mastering fine-grained kernel isolation using RuntimeClass, Sysctls, and cgroups v2 PSI/memory.high.

item.title: Hacking the Kubernetes Scheduler: Custom Plugins via Scheduling Framework, Volcano DRF Math, and Descheduler Dynamic Rebalancing
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why does the default Kubernetes scheduler deadlock when handling distributed AI model training and batch computing workloads? A deep architectural guide to customizing the scheduling core: exploring the 11 extension points of the official Scheduling Framework and CycleState data caching; dissecting Volcano's Dominant Resource Fairness (DRF) mathematical model and PodGroup state machine; implementing a production-grade Gang Scheduling (All-or-Nothing) plugin in Go with atomic Unreserve rollbacks; and executing safe, telemetry-driven cluster rebalancing using the Descheduler.

item.title: Kubernetes Storage Architecture: CSI Specification, Dynamic PV/PVC Provisioning, and StatefulSet Guarantees
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why was executing stateful databases on Kubernetes once treated as an operational taboo? A detailed architectural exploration of the cloud-native storage stack: the three-tier decoupling of StorageClass, PersistentVolume (PV), and PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC); the four lifecycle stages of the Container Storage Interface (CSI) specification (Provision, Attach, Stage, and Mount); and how StatefulSets leverage Headless Services and volumeClaimTemplates to maintain strict topological ordering and immutable data persistence.

item.title: Evolution of High-Concurrency Batching: From Continuous Batching to Chunked Prefill Eliminating Head-of-Line Blocking
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why does high-concurrency LLM serving suffer from severe latency spikes (TPOT jitter) even after eliminating memory fragmentation? A deep dive into the evolution from static batching to Orca's iteration-level continuous batching, the physical mechanics of head-of-line (HoL) blocking caused by long prefill bursts, and how Sarathi-Serve and vLLM leverage Chunked Prefill and decode piggybacking to flatten latency SLAs.

item.title: Evolution of Attention Kernels: From FlashAttention-1/2/3 SRAM Tiling to FlashInfer Unified Heterogeneous Serving
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why does standard self-attention trigger explosive HBM bandwidth bottlenecks as context scales? A comprehensive deep dive into the evolution of attention kernels: from FlashAttention-1's SRAM tiling and online softmax rescaling, to FlashAttention-2's loop inversion and warp-level zero-communication scheduling, to FlashAttention-3's Hopper TMA asynchronous copies and WGMMA warpgroups. Finally, we explore FlashInfer, the purpose-built LLM serving kernel library, revealing how native Paged KV cache indexing and Split-K parallel decoding rescue memory-bound decodes.

item.title: Production LLM Inference Engines Teardown: vLLM v1 vs. SGLang vs. TensorRT-LLM vs. llama.cpp Internals
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: From Python scheduling to asynchronous C++/Rust execution engines: an in-depth codebase teardown of the open-source world's top four inference engines. Comparing vLLM v1 zero-overhead multi-step scheduling, SGLang RadixAttention tree-based execution loops, TensorRT-LLM fused kernel pipelines with in-flight batching, and llama.cpp zero-dependency edge quantization, with an enterprise engineering decision matrix.

item.title: From model.generate() to the Roofline Model: The Physics of Prefill and Decode Divergence
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why do modern GPUs with hundreds of TFLOPS idle at less than 5% Tensor Core utilization during LLM inference? A first-principles exploration of the autoregressive loop, the Roofline model, and the mathematical divergence between compute-bound Prefill and memory-bound Decode.

item.title: Model Architecture Driving Inference Systems: From MHA/GQA to DeepSeek MLA Matrix Absorption and Memory Minimalism
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why does long-context inference hit an insurmountable wall despite aggressive software kernel and scheduling optimizations? A deep architectural exploration from classical MHA to GQA grouping compromises, culminating in DeepSeek's revolutionary Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA). We mathematically deconstruct low-rank latent projections, Decoupled RoPE, and the Matrix Absorption trick that allows serving engines to erase over 90% of multi-head Key-Value tensors from physical HBM during decode.

item.title: MoE Inference Internals: Expert Parallelism (EP), Dynamic Routing Gating, and All-to-All Overlapping
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why does the 671B DeepSeek-V3 activate only 37B parameters per token yet hit severe network latency walls during decode? A comprehensive deep dive into MoE inference internals: dynamic routing gating, auxiliary-loss-free balancing, Expert Parallelism (EP) All-to-Allv communication patterns, CUTLASS Grouped GEMM kernels, and DualPipe computation-communication overlapping.

item.title: Memory Virtualization in Inference Engines: PagedAttention and the Elimination of Memory Fragmentation
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why did early LLM serving systems waste 60% to 80% of GPU memory? A deep architectural exploration of vLLM's PagedAttention, logical-to-physical block mapping, zero-copy Copy-on-Write sharing, and non-contiguous CUDA attention kernels.

item.title: Prefill-Decode (P/D) Disaggregation Architecture: Compute-Memory Decoupling, RDMA Distributed KV Cache Transfer, and Cluster-Scale Pooling
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why does colocating Prefill and Decode on identical GPUs inevitably collapse performance under 128k long contexts and reasoning workloads? An in-depth architectural breakdown of Prefill-Decode (P/D) Disaggregation: compute vs. memory spatial isolation, GQA vs. DeepSeek MLA cross-node bandwidth modeling, GPUDirect RDMA zero-copy transfers, global KV pooling, and optimal P:D node ratio queuing theory.

item.title: Prefix Caching and State Reuse: From Hash Block Addressing to SGLang RadixAttention and Dynamic Tree Eviction
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why do inference engines repeatedly execute thousands of redundant prompt forward passes across multi-turn conversations and agent loops? A comprehensive dissection of Prefix Caching internals: from vLLM's hash-chained block indexing and boundary penalty, to SGLang's pioneering RadixAttention tree-structured prefix matching, node splitting, and LRU leaf eviction mechanics.

item.title: The Future of LLM Inference: Test-Time Compute, Reasoning Scheduling, and Tiered Cluster Storage
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: When autoregressive thinking tokens explode from hundreds to 128k in deep reasoning models, inference systems reach an epochal architectural inflection point. An in-depth investigation into Test-Time Compute infrastructure: mitigating KV Cache memory avalanches, tree-search (MCTS) speculative scheduling, reinforcement-learning-guided thinking budget governors, and cross-tier (SRAM/HBM/CXL/NVMe-oF) global KV pools.

item.title: AI Agent Memory Architecture: From Working Memory to Episodic Memory & Hierarchical Graph RAG
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why multi-million token context windows still fail to solve agent amnesia. A deep architectural dissection of the three-tier memory pyramid (Working, Episodic, and Long-Term Semantic Memory), Stanford Generative Agents reflection cycles, Letta (MemGPT) virtual paging, and runnable code with decay curves and hybrid retrieval.

item.title: Agentic Loops & State Machine Design: From ReAct to Deterministic Control Flows
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why prompt chaining and unconstrained ReAct loops fail in production AI systems. A deep architectural dissection of agent failure modes, Finite State Machine (FSM) graph flows, tool-calling resilience, and circuit breakers with runnable code.

item.title: Under the Hood of Browser-use (100k+ Stars): DOM Tree Distillation, Vision Grounding, and Production Web Agents
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why do traditional Selenium and Playwright scripts constantly break against modern web frontends? We dissect the architecture of Browser-use, the breakout open-source project with over 100k GitHub stars: DOM tree pruning, Set-of-Mark (SoM) visual coordinate grounding, state machine resilience, and end-to-end production recipes.

item.title: SGLang vs vLLM Architecture Showdown: RadixAttention, Structured Decoding, and High-Concurrency Benchmarks
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: A deep architectural breakdown between the dual titans of 2026 LLM inference: vLLM and SGLang. We dissect PagedAttention block paging versus RadixAttention tree-based prefix caching, compare scheduler-level structured decoding (JSON Schema) mechanics, and deliver rigorous benchmarks on an 8x H100 cluster alongside an enterprise decision framework.

item.title: Speculative Decoding in Production: From Draft Models to EAGLE-3 Dynamic Trees for 3x-5x Lossless Acceleration
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Why is autoregressive LLM decoding fundamentally bottlenecked by memory bandwidth? We dissect the mathematical proof of lossless distribution invariance in speculative decoding, trace its evolution from dual-model drafts to EAGLE-2/3 dynamic draft trees, and provide production configurations in vLLM and SGLang.

item.title: Test-Time Compute and GRPO in Practice: From PPO to Critic-Free Reinforcement Learning
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: A deep dive into the paradigm shift from pre-training scaling laws to test-time compute. We deconstruct the mathematical derivation of DeepSeek-R1's Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), critic-free architecture advantages, emergent self-reflection in long reasoning traces, and a complete, reproducible hands-on implementation.

item.title: Deploying 2026 Frontier Open Models On-Premise: Running DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3 on Multi-Node GPU Clusters
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Complete enterprise on-premise deployment guide for 1.6T - 2.8T MoE open-weight models: Hardware planning across GPU clusters, vLLM / SGLang distributed TP/PP configuration, FP8 dynamic quantization, and high-concurrency API gateway production setups.

item.title: 2026 Frontier Chinese LLMs Face-off: Kimi K3 vs GLM-5.3 vs DeepSeek-V4 Practical Benchmark & Architecture Selection
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: In-depth evaluation of China's top three frontier models in 2026: Kimi K3's 2.8T KDA attention, GLM-5.3's environment-scaled terminal execution, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro's 1.6T MoE software engineering prowess.

item.title: Beyond Simple Prompts: How Environment Scaling Is Reshaping Autonomous Agents in 2026
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Analyzing the major post-training paradigm shift of 2026: from text autoregression to multi-environment sandboxed RL. Deep dive into GLM-5.3's Terminal-Bench 3.0 breakthrough, Linux container orchestration, MCP protocol integration, and sandboxed agent engineering.

item.title: Demystifying 2026 Architecture Breakthroughs: How Kimi Delta Attention and DeepSeek MLA Conquered the Memory Wall
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: In the era of million-token context windows and trillion-parameter MoE, how KV Cache memory saturation became the core bottleneck. Deep mathematical and architectural breakdown of Moonshot's KDA and DeepSeek's MLA low-rank projections.

item.title: Evolving Models at Runtime: From Basic Reflection to MCTS-based Test-Time Compute
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: The potential of LLMs extends beyond pre-trained parameters. We dive deep into the frontier of Test-Time Compute: from Actor-Critic architecture to leveraging Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to decode the limits of Agent self-correction.

item.title: 2026 AI Paradigm Shift: Distributed Agent Orchestration & Evals to Combat Error Compounding
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: As LLMs move into complex enterprise production, how do we use distributed orchestration to combat error compounding? How do we build a statistically significant Evals system?

item.title: Deep Dive into AI Agent Architecture Evolution: From Prompt to Loop Engineering
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: A deep dive into the evolution of AI Agent architectures, exploring the 4-layer control plane extrapolation from Prompt, Context, Harness to Loop Engineering, and the 4 diseases of the ReAct architecture.

item.title: Agent Observability & Debugging: The Path from Black Box to White Box
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: AI Agents are not traditional software; we are debugging the reasoning process rather than the code itself. This article explores Trajectory Evaluation, LLM-as-a-Judge, and practical applications of mainstream Agent observability tools like LangSmith and Langfuse.

item.title: Context Engineering Guide: Managing Context Window like RAM
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: The hottest concept in 2026, evolving from Prompt Engineering to Context Engineering. A deep dive into managing the context window through Write, Select, Compress, and Isolate strategies to solve long-context amnesia, hallucinations, and context poisoning.

item.title: AI Coding Mastery: From 'Build Me an X' to Architecture Orchestrator
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Tools don't matter — methodology does. A deep dive into six core methods for mastering AI coding: Spec-Driven Development, Context Engineering, TDD Verification Loops, Multi-Agent Orchestration, Advanced Prompting, and Session Hygiene. Plus a 20+ tool matrix and five anti-patterns to avoid.

item.title: Reject Benchmark Hacking: How to Build an LLM Evaluation System for Your Business (LLM-as-a-Judge)
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Cease the obsession with writing more code; shift focus to deep evaluation thinking. We deconstruct LLM-as-a-Judge biases, the mathematics behind metrics, and reshaping CI/CD defenses for probabilistic systems.

item.title: LLM Quantization Hands-On Guide: Four Routes from Zero to Production
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Hands-on LLM quantization guide: download and run GGUF models (Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.gguf, llama.cpp, Ollama), quantize with AWQ/GPTQ, and deploy vLLM FP8 in production with copy-paste code.

item.title: The Critical Crossroads in AI History: Why Was *That One* Chosen Every Time?
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: A retrospective of six pivotal technology crossroads in AI's seventy-year history, dissecting the compute constraints, data dividends, and scalability logic behind each historical choice.

item.title: vLLM Online Inference in Production: From Architecture to Token Billing
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: A deep dive into vLLM's core architecture (PagedAttention, continuous batching, APC prefix caching, speculative decoding) for online serving. Covers OpenAI-compatible API setup, performance tuning, token billing systems, and complete Docker deployment with Prometheus monitoring.

item.title: Mapping the NVIDIA GPU Driver Stack: From Kernel Modules to Container Runtimes
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: A deep dive into the complex Linux NVIDIA GPU driver package structures. Understand the 5-layer architecture bridging nvidia-dkms, libnvidia, nvidia-utils, and driver metapackages. Plus, discover enterprise best practices and troubleshooting guides for 4 core deployment scenarios, including Docker model servers and DGX clusters.

item.title: LLM Quantization Precision Guide: From FP32 to 1-bit, How Much Quality Do You Actually Lose?
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: A comprehensive comparison of FP32, BF16, FP16, FP8, INT8, INT4, NF4, FP4, 1.58-bit and all major quantization formats — with real benchmark data and an in-depth FP8 vs INT8 technical analysis.

item.title: 7 Runtime Practices for Building AI Agents
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: Based on a real data analysis agent project, this article distills 7 reusable Agent Runtime practices covering state exposure, tool design, context control, guardrails, delegation, and trace-driven iteration.

item.title: MCP Deep Dive: The USB-C Port for AI
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: From architecture to hands-on development, a complete guide to the Model Context Protocol. Includes Python SDK tutorial, security mechanisms, and ecosystem comparison.

item.title: Skills Deep Dive: Give Your AI Coding Assistant a Professional Brain
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: From core principles to cross-platform practice, a complete guide to the AI coding assistant Skills system. Covers SKILL.md mechanics, six-platform comparison, hands-on writing guide, and best practices.

item.title: Prompt Engineering Practice Guide
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: An in-depth exploration of designing effective prompts to improve model output quality. Covers core techniques like Few-Shot, Chain-of-Thought, and ReAct with practical examples.

item.title: Deep Dive into 11 AI Foundation Model Trends in 2026

item.description: From Thinking reasoning modes to Agentic applications, a deep dive into the top 11 trends in AI foundation models for 2026.

item.title: Building AI Agent Applications from Scratch
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: A step-by-step guide to building intelligent agent systems using LangChain and the Claude API. Includes complete code and architecture design.

item.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in Practice: Strategies & Production Best Practices
item.dc:creator: ifnodoraemon
item.description: A complete guide on how to use retrieval-augmented generation strategies and production best practices. Covers vector databases, semantic chunking, ColBERT reranking, GraphRAG, and automated Ragas evaluation.

item.description: A comprehensive comparison of the top three foundation models in 2026, covering reasoning, coding, context windows, API pricing, and selection strategies.
